chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Fazzal, all together from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer, who said:

It reached Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) that Talha and Al-Zubayr were saying, 'Ali has no wealth.' He said, 'So that was grievous upon him, so he ordered his representatives to gather his harvest until when a year passed, they came to him, and they had gathered from the price of the harvest one hundred thousand dirhams.'

So it was displayed in front of him, and he sent for Talha and Al-Zubayr, and they came to him. He said to them both, 'This wealth, by Allah, is for me, there is no share for anyone else in it,' and it was verified in their eyes. He said, 'So they left from his presence, and they were saying, 'Indeed, he has wealth.'

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Ali)

ai.seo_question: How did Ali ibn Abi Talib prove his wealth to Talha and Al-Zubayr?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical demonstration of Imam Ali’s (AS) wealth to counter the political accusations of Talha and Al-Zubayr, who doubted his financial standing despite his status as Caliph. By presenting the accumulated harvest revenues (ghalla) of one hundred thousand dirhams, the Imam provided tangible proof of his personal assets, reinforcing his legitimacy and transparency in governance. This event underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam’s material sufficiency and his use of worldly resources as a means of establishing truth (haqq) in the face of opposition.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Fazzal, altogether from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘It (news) reached Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> that Talha and Al-Zubeyr were both saying, ‘There is not for Ali<sup>asws</sup>, any wealth’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So that was grievous upon him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> ordered his<sup>asws</sup> representatives that they should gather his<sup>asws</sup> harvest until when a year passes by, to bring it to him<sup>asws</sup>, and there had gathered from the price of the harvest, one hundred thousand Dirhams.

So he<sup>asws</sup> had it displayed in front of him<sup>asws</sup> and sent a messenger to Talha and Al-Zubayr. So he brought both of them to him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to them both: ‘This wealth, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, is for me<sup>asws</sup>, there not being a share for anyone else in it’, and they had both verified it’. So they both left from his<sup>asws</sup> presence, and they were both saying, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> does have wealth for him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Faddal all from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from abu Basir who has said the following: “’Amir al-Mu 5 minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was informed that Talhah and Zubayr say, ‘Ali has no assets . 5

He (the Imam) said, ‘It troubled him and he commanded his agents to collect his share of grains. They followed his instruction until the end of the year, then they brought it to him and it was worth one hundred thousand dirhams.

It was spread before him. He sent for Talhah and Zubayr. When they came he told them, “This asset by Allah belongs to me and no one has any share in it . 55 They had proof to verify it and they left saying, “He in fact does have assets . 55 5 55
